messages:
maya: Heads up — seeing a steady uptick in evictions in eu-west2 since ~00:30. Many small inference pods (0.25–1 GPU) are leaving fragmented shelves; reserved training jobs can't find contiguous 4GPU blocks.

dan: same. dashboard shows pending backlog for model-training-prod, backfills timing out.

evict-bot: [02:12 UTC] 47 evictions in eu-west2; common reason: Insufficient contiguous GPUs for pod spec. Pods evicted: model-training-prod-*, embedder-*.

kevin: here's a quick scrape of pending pods:
```
NAME                                 READY STATUS
model-training-prod-2026-03-20-01    0/1   Pending (0/4)
embedder-batch-rc-12                 0/1   Pending (0/1)
tiny-infer-xyz                       1/1   Running
```

anika: they're using mixed GPU requests (0.5, 1, 4) with strict podAntiAffinity to avoid noisy neighbors. That makes the binpack chooser spread them weirdly across nodes.

maya: we only recently rolled the soft-evict feature; maybe it lowered packing aggressiveness and prevented consolidation.

dan: cost angle: if we consolidate these tiny pods onto fewer nodes we can free ~20% of reserved capacity for 4GPU jobs; tradeoff is potential noisy-neighbor SLO regressions.

kevin: proposal: run the compacter job with coalesceThreshold=0.6 during a low-traffic window and allow transient preemptible consolidation (15m) to drain fragmented shelves. Also consider a short-lived taint on nodes with fragmentation>0.7 to guide scheduler away during the run.

anika: +1 for compacter. also suggest tweaking binpack heuristic to prefer same-GPU-size packing for large (>=4GPU) jobs so they get contiguous slots.

maya: action items: kevin to schedule compacter tonight 02:00 UTC (dry-run then live), dan to watch pending queue and abort if training SLOs spike, anika to prepare a canary rollout of the binpack heuristic to 2 nodes. I'll open an ops incident and link dashboards.

kevin: noted. starting a dry-run now and will post compacter diff and eviction deltas here.

maya: thanks — ping here with results. :thumbsup:
